notes: Sallow & Fen — a fictional heritage vegetable seed nursery on the Norfolk fen edge. Single-page site with: annotated botanical hero plate (hand-drawn inline SVG with stroke-draw animation), three-part argument with stats band, a 12-variety seed library with real horticultural data (prices, sow windows, germination percentages, batch numbers) and type/month filtering, a month-by-month sowing calendar wired to both the calendar panel and the filters, a five-step process section with a germination-certificate artefact, a £45/yr subscription with four-parcel timeline and sold-out status, three named founders, a seven-question FAQ, and a consultation/booking enquiry flow with human validation messages, error summary, character counter, conditional postcode field, localStorage draft autosave with restore banner, browser-only sent-enquiry records, print-copy and reset paths. Three policy dialogs (native <dialog>). All assets local: self-hosted Fraunces/Archivo/IBM Plex Mono woff2, 12 hand-authored botanical SVGs, favicon, og.png (1200x630, composed live from the page). SEO: single H1, semantic sections, descriptive meta/OG/Twitter tags, JSON-LD @graph (Organization+Store, WebSite, Product for the subscription, three Services matching the booking options, FAQPage matching the visible FAQ). Verified in-browser at 1440/768/390 (layout screenshots, no horizontal overflow at 390, mobile nav, scrollspy, calendar month switching, filters incl. empty state, full enquiry flow: empty-submit errors, bad postcode error, draft restore after an unplanned reload, successful submission with reference, sent list, privacy dialog). Keyboard: skip link, logical tab order audited, JS focus management on errors/success; trusted key events could not be dispatched by the embedded test browser, so button/radio activation was verified through the same click/submit event paths rather than raw key presses. prefers-reduced-motion is handled in CSS (animations/transitions/reveals/plate draw all collapse) but could not be emulated at runtime in this browser. Zero console errors observed across a full page walk; no external network requests. file:// was not directly openable by the embedded browser; the page uses no fetch/modules/CDN so it is expected to work from file:// (localStorage guarded with try/catch either way). Known limitations: enquiry/subscription are client-side only by design (storage-backed, nothing is transmitted); testimonials omitted deliberately in favour of verifiable process claims.
